items.stem: What is data leakage in a modelling project?

options.text: Information unavailable at prediction time leaking into training features, inflating performance
options.rationale: Correct: leakage uses future or target-derived information, overstating results.

options.text: A network security breach of the dataset
options.rationale: That is a different meaning of leak, not the modelling concept.
That is data loss, not leakage.
Feature count alone is not leakage.

items.explanation: Correct: leakage uses future or target-derived information, overstating results.

items.stem: Which TWO should be done before declaring a model ready for deployment? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Evaluate on a held-out test set not used for tuning
options.rationale: Correct: an untouched test set gives an unbiased estimate.

options.text: Plan what to monitor for drift after launch
options.rationale: Correct: monitoring is needed because performance degrades over time.

options.text: Tune hyperparameters on the test set and report that score
options.rationale: Tuning on the test set biases the reported performance.

options.text: Assume performance will stay constant indefinitely
options.rationale: Models degrade; this assumption is unsafe.

items.explanation: Correct: an untouched test set gives an unbiased estimate.

items.stem: A stakeholder says 'use ML to improve the business'. What is the first lifecycle step?

options.text: Frame a specific, measurable problem and success metric tied to a decision
options.rationale: Correct: problem framing precedes data and modelling work.

options.text: Immediately train several models and compare them
options.rationale: Modelling before framing wastes effort on the wrong target.
Data acquisition follows a framed problem.

options.text: Deploy a model and see what happens
options.rationale: Deployment is the last stage, not the first.

items.explanation: Correct: problem framing precedes data and modelling work.
